title: dedicated-capacity-weekly-prep-sr
content:
Weekly prep notes for dedicated capacity sync (SR)

Context:
- Recurring weekly planning for GPU pools, reservation renewals, and autoscaling tuning.
- Goal: validate 6-week forecast, surface blockers for reserved capacity purchases, and agree on autoscaling policy tweaks for p99 latency targets.
- Audience: capacity owners + product counterparts (Priya, Ben), SRE (Marcus), finance touchpoint if we need commitment changes.

Key numbers (current):
- Committed GPUs (current reserved): 320 A100-equivalent GPUs across pools (pool-alpha: 120, pool-beta: 80, pool-gamma: 120).
- Avg daily utilization (last 7d): 58% overall; p95 burst windows show 85% in pool-alpha.
- Avg queued requests during peak (last 3 days): 4.1k requests/minute, median queue wait ~420ms.
- Autoscale headroom configured: 20% on each pool (max nodes per pool set to double base), but scaling cooldown is 5m which causes short-term queuing during fast bursts.
- Upcoming renewals: 80 GPUs in pool-beta reserved contract expires 2026-03-18.

6-week forecast assumptions:
- New large customer onboarding (Sales CR-421) expected 2026-03-10 with projected sustained 15% increase in baseline token throughput (higher concurrency).
- Batch/embeddings job reorg (infra task) currently estimated to shift 40 GPUs worth of load off dedicated pools to on-demand in mid-March.
- Model rollout (release-engineering) to a larger-capacity quantized variant (v2.3-q5) should reduce per-token GPU time by ~8% starting 2026-03-15.

Preliminary recommendations:
1) Reservation decision for pool-beta (80 GPUs):
   - Option A: renew full 80 for another 12 months — pros: lower unit cost, reliable capacity for new customer; cons: commit if usage falls after batch reorg.
   - Option B: renew 40 GPUs and keep 40 on short-term on-demand — pros: flexibility; cons: higher expected unit cost and potential quota churn.
   - Recommend: Option B + revisit in 6 weeks after onboarding stabilization. Rationale: new customer profile uncertain; batch reorg may free capacity.

2) Autoscaling policy tweaks:
   - Reduce scale cooldown from 5m -> 90s for pool-alpha to respond faster to rapid spikes.
   - Add aggressive pre-warm rule for traffic patterns at 09:00-11:00 PST and 18:00-20:00 PST (observed daily spikes) to pre-allocate 15% headroom.
   - Implement a transient queue threshold: if queue > 800 req/min for >60s, temporarily increase max nodes by additional 10% (temporary buffer) and notify on-call.
   - Tradeoffs: faster scaling increases cost; need to limit for non-critical workloads.

3) Monitoring and alerting changes:
   - Create short-term dashboard: reserved-utilization, queue-length, scale-events, scale-latency (time from scale trigger to available capacity).
   - Add SLO guardrail: if p99 latency > 1.2x target for >10m during scale, trigger manual review.

Open questions / items to surface in sync:
- Sales to confirm CR-421 SLA expectations and projected QPS pattern (burst vs sustained). (Action: Priya)
- Finance: what’s the acceptable variance for reserved spend this quarter if we go Option B? (Action: Ben)
- Release team: confirm actual performance improvement and timeline for v2.3-q5 (Action: Elena).
- Batch job reorg ETA and how many GPUs freed (Action: Marcus).

Action items (owner — due):
- Priya Iyer — confirm CR-421 expected onboarding date and traffic profile (by 2026-03-05).
- Ben Thompson — run cost sensitivity for Option A vs B (12mo commit vs 6+on-demand) and share by 2026-03-06.
- Marcus Li — prototype cooldown change in staging for pool-alpha and run two synthetic spike tests (by 2026-03-04).
- Elena Park — confirm model rollout perf delta and compatibility with current runtime kernels (by 2026-03-07).
- Sofia Reyes (me) — prepare short dashboard template and a one-pager recommendation for pool-beta decision (by 2026-03-08).

Meeting agenda (15–30m):
1) Quick numbers (Sofia) — 3m: current utilization + renewals
2) Sales confirmation & timeline (Priya) — 5m
3) Finance sensitivity (Ben) — 5m
4) Autoscale changes proposal (Marcus + Sofia) — 7m
5) Decide reservation approach (vote) + follow-ups — 5m

Notes for manager 1:1 follow-up (if time):
- Recommend provisional approval for Option B with explicit re-eval date (2026-03-22).
- Ask for pre-approval on up to 10% temporary spend over budget for emergency scale during first-week onboarding.

Risks / mitigation:
- Risk: new customer traffic higher than projected leading to p99 violations during scale windows. Mitigation: temporary burst pool (on-demand) with alert-triggered auto-top-up and manual override.
- Risk: commit cost locked in while workload drops. Mitigation: staggered reserve + buyback option discussion with procurement.

Notes to self / scratch ideas:
- Explore short-term convertible reservations with cloud provider (if available) — could buy now and convert down later.
- Align with product for a soft cap on concurrency for new customers during initial ramp to protect SLOs.
- Follow up on GH-PR-1287 (scheduler improvements) that might reduce scale latency by ~20s if merged.

Short-term timeline (next 2 weeks):
- 3/03: run staging spike tests with reduced cooldown (Marcus)
- 3/05: Sales confirms CR-421 profile (Priya)
- 3/06: Finance sensitivity (Ben)
- 3/08: recommendation doc + dashboard (Sofia)
- 3/10: anticipated onboarding (contingent)

End of notes.
